name: Tucson Unified School District
intake_notes: Recent news: superintendent announced new SPED initiative 4/5

enrichment.sped_program_notes: TUSD operates a large continuum of SPED services including self-contained programs, resource support, and related services (SLP, OT, PT, etc.) across ~80+ school sites. At this scale, the IEP team ecosystem is complex and a strong candidate for Journify's multi-role platform (teachers, therapists, case managers). Likely uses a major IEP platform (e.g., Frontline or SEIS-AZ) — Journify integrates with both.
enrichment.region_context: Tucson Unified is Arizona's second-largest district, serving a diverse urban/suburban population in Pima County. The district has a historically high proportion of students qualifying for Title I and Medicaid-reimbursable special education services.
enrichment.recent_initiatives: Superintendent announced a new SPED initiative on 4/5 (per intake notes). TUSD has also been under a long-running federal desegregation consent decree (Mendoza v. TUSD), which historically intersects with equity obligations in special education service delivery.
enrichment.pain_points: 1) A newly announced SPED initiative signals active internal pressure to improve systems — likely paperwork, compliance, and/or service delivery. 2) At ~44k enrollment, TUSD likely employs 200+ SPED staff with significant IEP documentation burden across multiple schools. 3) Arizona has faced SPED staffing shortages statewide, amplifying caseload pressure on existing staff. 4) Federal oversight history (consent decree) raises stakes for audit-readiness and documentation accuracy — areas where Journify directly reduces risk.
enrichment.fit_reasoning: TUSD is a compelling enterprise-tier target with a strong thematic fit. Enrollment at 44k sits just at the upper edge of Journify's sweet spot — still very winnable but procurement cycles may be longer. The superintendent's newly announced SPED initiative (4/5) is a meaningful warm signal suggesting active investment and internal momentum. The district's scale (~6,400 estimated IEPs), compliance history, and statewide staffing pressure all map directly to Journify's core value props (paperwork automation, audit-readiness, goal tracking). Score is held to 62 rather than higher due to: (1) zero resolved intent signals — no webinar attendance, RFP, or whitepaper download to confirm active buying interest; (2) no named SPED decision-maker identified yet; (3) large-district procurement risk. Recommend prioritizing contact discovery for the SPED Director and framing outreach around the superintendent's SPED initiative as the hook.

email_draft.subject: Tucson's 6,300 IEPs, half the paperwork | Journify
email_draft.body:
Dr. Trujillo's April 5th announcement of a new SPED initiative caught our attention. When a district the size of TUSD makes that kind of public commitment, the pressure lands squarely on the case managers and therapists doing the daily work across 80+ sites.

At roughly 6,400 IEPs, your SPED staff are running one of the largest documentation operations in Arizona, across self-contained programs, resource rooms, and related services, likely without a shared system tying the whole team together. Teachers report saving more than four hours per day using Journify, which integrates directly with your existing IEP system rather than replacing it. That time goes back to students, not screens.

Open to a 20-minute conversation this week to see whether this maps to what Dr. Trujillo's initiative is trying to solve?
email_draft.hook_summary: Superintendent's April 5 SPED initiative announcement used as the district-specific hook.
